issues.description: The /\dm?s/i fast-path regex is an over-approximation that can match digits adjacent to s/ms inside url() or quoted strings.
issues.detail: All three reviewers note the pattern matches substrings like url(foo1s.png) or "abc1ms". Correctness is preserved because false positives only trigger the slow valueParser path. Worth a one-line comment noting the regex is a deliberate over-approximation gate, not a precise time-token detector.

issues.description: Fast-path regex and valueParser walk are two implementations of the same predicate with no documented invariant linking them.
issues.detail: The module now has two notions of has-time that must stay in lockstep as CSS time units evolve. Document the invariant (regex-false implies no time token) near the regex, or extract a named helper, so future maintainers updating unit support update both sites. Test fixtures covering url(), custom properties containing ms, and quoted strings would harden the contract.

synthesis.summary: The panel unanimously accepts this as a sound, narrow performance fix: a cheap regex pre-filter short-circuits the expensive valueParser call when no time-like token is present in the declaration value. Correctness is preserved because the regex is a deliberate over-approximation — false positives still hit the authoritative slow path. The only consensus concerns are documentation-level: the regex matches digits adjacent to s/ms inside url() or strings, and the implicit contract between the fast-path and the parser should be stated so the two predicates stay in lockstep as time units evolve. No blockers; ship with a clarifying comment and a couple of edge-case fixtures.
